Definition: from Σέλευκος (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria:--Seleucia.
BiblicalUsage: Seleucia is the port where Paul and Barnabas first sailed out, being sent forth by the Holy Ghost. They departed unto Seleucia, and from thence they sailed to Cyprus.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Seleucia is the doorway of the mission to the nations — the Holy Ghost sent them, and the ship left from here.
